$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

A stale temp from a crash makes create_new fail with AlreadyExists, so remove a leftover temp first. clients.rs uses a fixed json.tmp with File::create, which does not set mode on an existing file.

Q3 race: two processes starting on the same link dir could both see NotFound and rename over each other, so the last rename wins while the first serves its key. create_new today sends the second creator to read(). architect.run_scope: orchestra only (one app). ROADMAP.md is in no slice; the orchestrator updates it at close. No protocol/ change: the offer JSON and the handshake are P3a's, unchanged; the new link-* event names go from the shell to the webview only and are not wire events.
architect.rationale: Single-loop, one branch, slices run in order s1 -> s2 -> s3 -> s4. The file sets ARE disjoint (core link files / shell Rust plus Cargo files / frontend / docs), but a diamond needs 3+ slices whose done_when stands alone and that consume nothing from each other. Here s3 consumes s2's IPC contract (command names, DTO shapes, event names), s4 records s1-s3's as-built behaviour and test counts, and only s1 is truly independent. Two parallel-safe pieces do not earn a graph. Fixing the contract in this plan (notes.ipc_contract) lets s3 be written against the plan, but its review still needs s2 on disk. Risk tags: s1 HIGH - it rewrites the host private key write path (sensitive material) and changes the confirm/timeout state machine, whose race a test can only partly see. s2 HIGH - unsafe Win32 FFI that reads and writes the host private key, the boundary that keeps the pairing secret out of IPC text (no test can prove there is no other leak path), thread/lock rules where a mistake is a deadlock (stop() from a callback) or a 30 s main-thread hang, and Cargo.lock. It does not touch tauri.conf.json or capabilities/** (the CSP pin only reads the file via include_str). s3 HIGH - the confirm dialog is the user's trust decision (default scopes, Accept failure, expiry) and it renders the secret-bearing QR; with no component-test harness (G11) that behaviour is visible only to a reader and to the owner's hand test. s4 LOW - prose only, no sensitive data, no file shared with another slice; grep done_when plus a scope check is enough. No file appears in two slices: lib.rs and Cargo.lock only in s2, App.tsx only in s3, CLAUDE.md and protocol/README.md only in s4. Disagreements with the scout, flagged and not plan-changing: (1) the risk 'CLAUDE.md:96-97 still says add its origin' is stale. P3a s4 already rewrote it: orchestra/CLAUDE.md:96-99 now says the link needs no origin, and grep 'add its origin' returns 0. No slice edits that line. (2) 'host_key must never reach the webview' must be read as the PRIVATE key (SecretKey). PairingOffer.host_key (pairing.rs:98-99) is the host's static PUBLIC key and is meant to be in the QR. (3) Verified rather than trusted: on_pairing_request returns at once and the conn thread polls a sync_channel(1) until the deadline (conn.rs:326-352). stop() joins accept, then connection threads (server.rs:355-370). Every LinkHost query except open_pairing goes through shared() and fails NotRunning when the link is stopped (server.rs:380-442), so list_clients/revoke/set_scopes do NOT work while the link is off. LinkConfig is owned by LinkHost with no setter, so changing binds means building a new LinkHost. Also verified: ClientStore is pub with open/list/set_scopes/revoke (clients.rs:113-212); Client has no last-seen field and LinkLog has no connect event; the stored name is already clipped to 128 bytes (clients.rs:21,183,240), but PendingPairing.client_name is not (conn.rs:333-336); Scope has no serde (wire/mod.rs:39-45); windows-sys 0.61.2 is in Cargo.lock and has CredWriteW/CredReadW/CredFree/CredDeleteW, CRED_TYPE_GENERIC, CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE and CRED_MAX_CREDENTIAL_BLOB_SIZE=2560 under Win32_Security_Credentials (checked in the local registry copy). desktop-release.yml builds the shell on windows-latest and macos-latest, at tag time only.

alternatives: Diamond s1 || s2 || s3, then s4: the file sets are disjoint, but s3 consumes s2's contract and s1 is the only free slice. The saving is small and a fan-in risk is added; rejected.
Two runs (Rust now, UI next): ships commands nobody can click and leaves the owner's hand test for later; rejected.

decisions_for_gate.title: Keyring approach
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Call Win32 Credential Manager directly from the shell: windows-sys 0.61 with the Win32_Security_Credentials feature, as a [target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies] entry in desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml. 0.61.2 is already in Cargo.lock, so no new crate is added; the lock gains one dependency edge on the orchestra package. New module desktop/src-tauri/src/keyring.rs: CredentialKeyProvider { target: String } implements KeyProvider. load_or_create: CredReadW(target, CRED_TYPE_GENERIC). Found with a 32-byte blob -> SecretKey::from_bytes. Wipe the CREDENTIALW blob before CredFree. Found with any other length -> KeyError::BadFile, never overwritten (same fail-closed rule as the file). ERROR_NOT_FOUND -> SecretKey::generate, CredWriteW (CRED_TYPE_GENERIC, CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE: survives logoff, does not roam), then read back and return what is stored, which narrows the two-process first-start race to the read-back. Any other failure -> KeyError::Io(ErrorKind::Other) (no new KeyError variant). Target name: 'com.telosrg.orchestra/link/host_key' (the bundle identifier). The 32 raw bytes are stored as the blob, well under 2560. Tests use a unique per-test target and CredDeleteW afterwards; they never touch the real one. Consequence to state in the UI copy: if the user deletes this credential, the host gets a new key and every paired phone is refused as 'host key changed' (the protocol pins the host key) until it is paired again. Unverified: that CredWriteW succeeds on the windows-latest runner; if it does not, the round-trip test is ignored with a written reason and run locally.
alternatives: keyring crate 4.2.0 (MIT OR Apache-2.0), Windows-only target dependency with default-features=false: less unsafe code of ours, but v4 split into keyring-core plus per-store crates. Which features select the Windows store under default-features=false was not read (scout unknown). It adds keyring-core, windows-native-keyring-store and byteorder to the lock. Take it if the owner prefers no unsafe in the shell; the builder must then read the crate source first.
Keep FileKeyProvider on the desktop for P3b and defer the keyring: zero risk, but it contradicts protocol/README.md:73 and the ROADMAP P3b bullet; rejected.

decisions_for_gate.title: An existing host_key file: migrate or keep?
decisions_for_gate.recommend: No migration, and the file is left alone. Before P3b no desktop build ever constructed a LinkHost (P3a added no shell wiring; desktop/src-tauri/src has no link code), so no desktop install can have link/host_key or a phone paired against it. On Windows the provider never reads or deletes link/host_key. On other OSes FileKeyProvider keeps using it (G4).
alternatives: Import link/host_key into the keyring on first start and delete the file: code that serves no install that exists; rejected.
Import it and keep the file: two copies of a private key; rejected.

decisions_for_gate.title: link/config.json
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Path: app_data_dir/link/config.json, beside clients.json (and host_key on non-Windows). Schema: {"schema":1, "enabled":false, "port":47800, "binds":["127.0.0.1"], "firewall_notice_seen":false}. binds are bare IP strings; the one port is shared by every bind. A missing file means these defaults, so the link is off. An unknown schema or a file that does not parse -> link off, the file left alone, the settings read-only with 'written by a newer Orchestra' or 'could not be read'. This is the clients.json rule. The atomic write is a small private helper in desktop/src-tauri/src/link_config.rs: temp file, write_all, sync_all, rename. It copies the clients.rs:213-225 pattern and takes no core dependency. enabled PERSISTS: at setup, if enabled, the shell starts the link on a background thread. The point of the link is that a phone reconnects without a click on the desktop. The header shows the link state at all times. A saved bind that no longer exists on any interface (DHCP changed, Tailscale down) is skipped at start. The link starts on the binds that remain, and link_status.missing lists the skipped ones for the UI ('192.168.1.20 is not on this computer right now'). The config is NOT rewritten, so the address can come back. If no bind remains, the link stays off with that reason. A start error (port busy, unreadable clients.json, keyring failure) leaves the link off, keeps enabled as saved, and shows the error with Retry.
alternatives: enabled does not persist (off on every launch): safer against forgotten exposure, but the phone cannot reconnect after a desktop restart until someone clicks. Take it if the owner values that.
Fail the whole start when any saved bind is missing: simpler and stricter, but a laptop that changed Wi-Fi silently loses the link, including Tailscale.

decisions_for_gate.title: Bind choices, interface enumeration, port policy
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Choices are enumerated, never free text. Use the if-addrs crate 0.15.0 (MIT OR BSD-3-Clause, updated 2026-02-08, about 31M downloads; deps libc on unix and windows-sys 0.61.2, which is already in the lock). The list is IPv4 only: 127.0.0.1 (always, 'This computer only'); 100.64.0.0/10 labelled 'Tailscale'; RFC1918 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16 labelled 'Local network'; anything else 'Other'. Link-local 169.254/16 is excluded. 0.0.0.0, :: and their IPv4-mapped forms are never listed. link_set_config also re-checks in Rust that each bind parses, is in the current enumeration or is 127.0.0.1, and passes core validate_binds, so the core would refuse an unspecified address at start anyway. Port: one fixed, user-editable port (default 47800, range 1024-65535) for all binds. Never 0 (ephemeral), because a phone stores ip:port from the QR and must find the host again after a restart. A busy port is a start error naming the port, with the port field next to it.
alternatives: local-ip-address 0.6.13 (MIT OR Apache-2.0): adds neli on Linux; no advantage here.
GetAdaptersAddresses through windows-sys plus getifaddrs through libc by hand: no crate, but two unsafe FFI paths and one uncompiled off Windows; rejected.
Free-text address with validation: invites typos and 0.0.0.0 attempts; rejected for v1.
IPv6 binds (Tailscale fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, ::1): the core supports them; the UI can add them later.

decisions_for_gate.title: Firewall notice
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Shown when the user first saves an enabled config containing a non-loopback bind while firewall_notice_seen is false. The save is held until they press Continue, which sets firewall_notice_seen=true in the same write. link_set_config refuses a first non-loopback enable without the flag, so the order is enforced in Rust and not only in the UI. Windows wording: 'Windows may ask whether Orchestra can use the network. Tick Private networks and choose Allow. If you choose Cancel, Windows adds a rule that blocks Orchestra, and your phone cannot connect until you allow it under Windows Security > Firewall & network protection > Allow an app through firewall.' macOS: 'macOS may ask whether Orchestra can accept incoming connections. Choose Allow.' Linux: 'If a firewall such as ufw is on, allow TCP port <port>.' Loopback-only never shows it. Whether Windows classes the Tailscale adapter as Private or Public is unverified, so the copy does not claim it.
alternatives: Create a firewall rule programmatically (INetFwPolicy2 COM, needs elevation) or from the installer: the installer route belongs to R1 (release, ops gate); rejected for P3b.
Show the notice on every non-loopback enable: noisy; rejected.

decisions_for_gate.title: The confirm dialog
decisions_for_gate.recommend: One request is shown at a time. The pairing window is single-use, so there is normally at most one, and Open pairing is disabled while a request is pending. The shell keeps a small list anyway, and the UI shows the first with 'N more waiting'. The shell's on_pairing_request only pushes PendingView { id, client_name, fingerprint, expires_at = now + confirm_timeout } into a leaf mutex and emits link-pairing-request. It never calls LinkHost, because stop() from that thread self-joins and deadlocks. The dialog (role=alertdialog, rendered at App level over either view) shows the name as text: React escapes it; CSS ellipsis; title attribute for the full name. The core caps the name at 128 bytes and strips control characters (G12), and the UI truncates to 64 characters for display. The fingerprint is shown in monospace with 'Check that your phone shows the same code', and there is a countdown. Scope checkboxes: read and answer checked, control and land unchecked, with one-line descriptions from the README table. Accept with no scope at all is refused. Accept and Reject are the buttons; Escape rejects. Accept failure is explicit. UnknownPairing -> 'Your phone stopped waiting. Open pairing again.' (this covers the P3a race and a dropped connection). StoreError::Full -> '32 devices are paired. Remove one first.' Any other error -> the core message. On timeout the dialog turns to 'This request expired' with Close, and the shell drops entries past expires_at when it reads the list.
alternatives: Queue and show every request: a pending request holds one of 16 slots for 300 s, so a list invites slot exhaustion; rejected.
Auto-reject a second request: impossible from the callback (it must not call LinkHost) and needs a worker thread; not worth it at a 1-request steady state.

decisions_for_gate.title: Devices panel and placement
decisions_for_gate.recommend: A 'Devices' button in the header, next to Open project, and a link-state pill ('Link off' / 'Link on - 2 addresses' / 'Link error'). With no router, App keeps a view state 'work' | 'devices', and 'devices' replaces the three columns with the Devices panel, which has a Back button. The panel has three parts. (a) Link settings: an enable switch, address checkboxes from link_interfaces, the port field, Save, and status, missing addresses and errors. (b) Pair a phone: opens the QR dialog, enabled only while the link is running and no request is pending. (c) Paired devices: name, fingerprint, paired_at date, and the four scope checkboxes (a change saves at once through link_set_scopes, and the last scope cannot be unchecked; read is explained as required for status). Remove asks first ('Remove <name>? It is disconnected now and must pair again.'), then link_revoke. No last-seen: Client has no such field and LinkLog has no connect event, so it needs a core change (NOT DOING). paired_at is shown instead. Devices are listed and editable while the link is OFF: with no running host the shell opens ClientStore::open(link_dir) itself, under its lifecycle mutex, so a lost phone can be revoked without opening a socket. While running, it goes through LinkHost. The panel must work at the 640 px window minimum.
alternatives: Devices read-only while the link is off: simpler, but revoking a lost phone would require turning on the network first; rejected.
A modal settings sheet instead of a view swap: the device list does not fit at 640 px; rejected.

decisions_for_gate.title: Tests and the CSP pin
decisions_for_gate.recommend: No jsdom, happy-dom or @testing-library, so no package.json or package-lock change. All UI logic goes into a pure module, desktop/src/link.ts, tested in desktop/src/link.test.ts under vitest's node environment: the link view reducer, default scopes, scope toggling that keeps at least one, needsFirewallNotice(config, prev), interface labels, display truncation, countdown formatting and expiry, Accept-error text mapping, and qrDataUrl. ipc.test.ts gains decoder tests for the new DTOs and events, including rejecting a payload that carries a 'secret' field. Rust shell tests run in windows-workspace: config default, round trip, unknown schema left alone, temp file then rename; bind validation (0.0.0.0, ::, ::ffff:0.0.0.0, a port out of range, an address not in the enumeration); interface classification; the PairingView carries no secret; the QR SVG has no style; a Credential Manager round trip on a test target (same key on the second call, BadFile on a 31-byte blob). The CSP pin is a cfg(test) test named csp_pinned in desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs. It reads ../tauri.conf.json with include_str, parses it with serde_json, and asserts app.security.csp equals exactly "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost". tauri.conf.json is not modified.
alternatives: Add vitest component tests (jsdom plus @testing-library/react, or happy-dom): covers the dialogs' states, but adds devDependencies, a vitest environment config and lock churn. Versions were not chosen by the scout. Then s3 also owns orchestra/desktop/package.json, orchestra/desktop/package-lock.json and orchestra/desktop/vite.config.ts.
The CSP pin as a vitest test importing the JSON: runs on ubuntu on every push, but reaches outside src/ for tsc; rejected in favour of the Rust include_str.

decisions_for_gate.title: P3a follow-ups folded in
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Three, all in core s1. (a) host_key atomic (P3a medium; the goal). Write to a unique sibling temp host_key.tmp-<8 random hex>, created with create_new and mode 0600 on Unix, then write_all and sync_all. Publish with fs::hard_link(tmp, host_key): AlreadyExists -> another creator won, so read theirs (the no-clobber property create_new gives today is kept). Remove the temp in every case. A crash leaves at most a stray temp, never a short host_key. An existing short file stays BadFile and is never overwritten. (b) Cap and clean the pairing client name at the seam: conn.rs passes the name through the same clip used by ClientStore::add (128 bytes on a char boundary, trimmed) and also drops control characters, before the PendingEntry and the PendingPairing are built. H2's terminal prompt benefits too. (c) The confirm/timeout race. When await_confirmation's loop ends without a decision, it removes its pending entry. If the entry was already gone, the host took it: it then waits briefly (recv_timeout of about 1 s) for the decision already sent and honours it, so the stored client gets welcome, or Rejected closes. That removal is the single linearisation point, and 'stored but never welcomed' is gone. remove_pending returns whether it removed.
alternatives: Only (a), the goal's item: leaves the UI showing names up to 4 MiB and a device listed that never got welcome.
Also stop() joining call workers, revoke-during-connect snapshot, pre-auth buffering, limiter IPv6 cap, KK timing, zeroize docs: none affects the desktop UI; NOT DOING.

decisions_for_gate.title: Shell lifecycle and threading rules (builder contract)
decisions_for_gate.recommend: LinkState is managed state holding: a lifecycle Mutex<()> that serialises start, stop, reconfigure and offline ClientStore edits; a slot Mutex holding Option<Arc<LinkHost>>, the loaded config, last_error and missing; and a leaf pending Mutex<Vec<PendingView>>. Every command that starts, stops or reconfigures is async with spawn_blocking (the commands.rs:42-47 pattern). No shell mutex other than lifecycle is held across LinkHost::stop. Callbacks only push to pending and emit; LinkLog lines go to eprintln (they carry ids and method names only by design). Reconfigure = stop the old host, build a new LinkHost::new(Arc::clone of sessions, LinkConfig{binds, host_name, link_dir, storage: status.clone()}, provider, callbacks), then start. host_name is COMPUTERNAME on Windows, HOSTNAME elsewhere, falling back to 'Orchestra', clipped to 64. With no app data dir (data_dir None at lib.rs:32) the link is unavailable and says so. Exit: RunEvent::Exit must not wait on a 30 s join. The hook signals stop on a spawned thread and waits at most 2 s, and the builder confirms whether managed state is dropped at exit (Drop for LinkHost calls stop). Emitted events: link-pairing-request, link-status-changed, link-devices-changed (after confirm, revoke and set_scopes, and on LinkLog::Paired/Revoked).
alternatives: Add a core API that lets LinkHost be reconfigured or queried while stopped: cleaner for H2, but it widens a core seam P3a just closed; rejected for P3b.

decisions_for_gate.title: Owner hand test (human-read; the phone side is A1)
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Nothing can pair end to end until A1 (no phone Noise client). After s3, the owner runs 'cd orchestra/desktop && npm run tauri dev' on Windows and clicks through the following. (1) Header pill shows 'Link off'. Open Devices. (2) Tick 127.0.0.1 only, port 47800, enable, Save: no firewall notice, and the pill turns to 'Link on - 1 address'. (3) Pair a phone: a QR appears with the host name, 127.0.0.1:47800, the loopback hint and a countdown. The QR scans with any phone camera app to JSON with v, host_id, host_name, addrs, host_key, secret and expires_at, and the image renders under the CSP (no console CSP violation in devtools). (4) Close the dialog, reopen: a new code. (5) Tick a LAN or Tailscale address, Save: the firewall notice appears first; Continue, then Windows' own prompt may appear (choose Allow, Private). (6) The paired-devices list is empty, with an empty-state line. (7) Disable, Save: the pill turns to 'Link off' within a few seconds and the UI stays responsive. (8) Quit with the link on: the app exits in about 2 s or less. (9) Restart with the link left enabled: it auto-starts. (10) Windows Credential Manager > Windows Credentials shows 'com.telosrg.orchestra/link/host_key'. (11) Resize to 640 px: the Devices view is usable. The confirm dialog and device editing cannot be reached by hand without a client. They are covered by link.test.ts and core tests/link.rs, and the full click-through moves to A1.
alternatives: A dev-only fake pairing request command (gated on debug_assertions) so the owner can see the confirm dialog before A1: no new files beyond link.rs and lib.rs; offer only if the owner wants it.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.issue: load() validates only the schema and the field types, so a config.json with port 0 or 22 (u16, below MIN_PORT) loads as valid, and apply() binds settings.port as it is: {"schema":1,"enabled":true,"port":0,"binds":["127.0.0.1"],"firewall_notice_seen":false} auto-starts on an ephemeral port that changes every launch, against G7's 'never 0'. Likewise a hand-edited enabled file with a LAN bind and firewall_notice_seen:false auto-starts exposed with no notice. Only validate() writes the file, so this needs a hand edit; the fix is to treat port < 1024 as Unreadable at load, as port 70000 already is.

Online edits (revoke, set_scopes) run on a cloned Arc<LinkHost> outside lifecycle, by G13's design. If link_set_config's apply() stops that host and starts a new one between the core's shared() and its store lock inside LinkHost::revoke, the old store writes clients.json after the new host has loaded it. The new host keeps the revoked client in memory until its next restart. The window is a few instructions wide and would need a double action in the UI; noted for the core's revoke-during-reconfigure follow-up.

CredWriteW overwrites an existing credential, so if two processes start for the first time at once, both read None and both write. The read-back narrows this but does not close it, which is what G2 accepted. Recorded so nobody later reads 'read back' as no-clobber.

save() leaves config.json.tmp behind if write_all, sync_all or rename fails. It is harmless, because the next save truncates it and load never reads it, but the core's atomic writers remove their temp on every path.

findings.title: Initial link status can overwrite a newer link-status-changed event
findings.detail: App.tsx subscribes onLinkStatusChanged, then dispatches the linkStatus() snapshot after the whole Promise.all resolves. linkReducer 'status' overwrites unconditionally. If auto_start (lib.rs:100, background thread) finishes between linkStatus() returning and Promise.all resolving, the event (running:true) lands first and the stale snapshot (enabled:true, running:false) replaces it: pill reads 'Link off', Pair a phone is disabled, LinkSettings says 'on but not running' with no Retry and Save not dirty, until some later status event. Timing-dependent and narrow (start is usually done before the webview loads), so a note. Fix: ignore the snapshot if an event already arrived, or fetch link status after subscribing in its own step.

findings.title: Modals do not keep keyboard focus inside
findings.detail: PairingRequest and PairingDialog focus the dialog div on mount and set aria-modal, but there is no Tab trap and the background is not inert: Shift+Tab from the confirm dialog reaches the header Devices button behind the overlay. Focus is not restored on close. The firewall notice and remove confirm are inline role=alertdialog blocks that do not receive focus, and at 640x480 the firewall notice can render below the fold after Save. No trust bypass: Enter on the dialog div does nothing, Escape only rejects, and the overlay blocks pointer input. Worth fixing before or at the G14 hand test.

findings.title: Save or Retry before link_interfaces resolves drops every saved bind without a note
findings.detail: LinkSettings.present() filters against interfaces, which is [] until linkInterfaces() resolves (or forever if it errored). gone is suppressed when interfaces is empty, so no note shows. Untick 'Turn the link on' and Save in that window -> link_set_config {enabled:false, binds:[]} is accepted by validate (empty binds allowed when disabled) and config.json loses its binds. Retry uses present(status.binds) the same way. Recoverable by re-ticking; no exposure. Fix: disable Save/Retry until interfaces have loaded.

findings.title: Link load is in the app's one Promise.all
findings.detail: linkStatus() and linkPending() join the initial Promise.all in App.tsx, so a link decode failure would also stop sessions, inbox, tasks and projects from loading. The contracts match today (checked field by field), so this is a robustness note only.

findings.title: pill-text-on/off/error classes are not defined
findings.detail: LinkSettings uses className pill-text-${tone} on the status line; App.css defines no such class. Cosmetic only.

findings.title: Deviation judged a sound reading, not a contradiction of G6
findings.detail: G6's 'skipped and reported, config not rewritten' governs start (apply/split_binds), which is unchanged. G7 (approved) has link_set_config refuse any bind not in the current enumeration, so a user save can only carry present binds. The alternative, refusing every save while an address is gone, would stop the user turning the link off while Tailscale is down. dirty compares present(binds) to present(status.binds), so no save happens without a user change, and the note 'a save removes it from the list' is shown before Save.
